headline: Leaning lower, with big swings likely
text: US futures are down today (S&P −1.03%, Nasdaq −2.09%), with Europe lower and Asia mostly up.
Helping: Asia, 10-year yield, Copper, Stocks above 200-day. Weighing: Europe, S&P 500 vs 200-day, VIX, VIX curve.

Expect a jumpy session: the VIX is high at 29.2, SPY options gamma is negative (dealers' hedging makes moves bigger), the VIX curve is inverted. Gaps and reversals are common in these conditions, so a small early move says little.
Today's data: GDP at 08:30 New York time (previous 3.8); PCE inflation at 08:30 New York time (previous 3.6). The first minutes after a release can whip both ways.
Options price a typical day of about ±1.8% for the S&P 500 (about 7,024–7,287); historically about 82% of days stay inside that.
On past days with VIX between 25 and 30 (since 1990, 871 days), the next session closed higher 52% of the time (all days: 54%), with a typical move of 0.9% (all days: 0.5%).

drivers.name: US futures
drivers.note: S&P −1.03% · Nasdaq −2.09% vs the last close. Live index futures.

drivers.name: Dollar index
drivers.note: A sharply stronger dollar usually weighs on US stocks (tighter money, weaker overseas earnings).

drivers.name: 10-year yield
drivers.note: At 4.84%. Fast-rising yields hurt growth and tech stocks; falling yields help them.

drivers.name: WTI oil
drivers.note: $83.72. A big oil jump feeds inflation worries; energy stocks move with it.

drivers.name: Gold
drivers.note: $3556. A strong gold bid often means investors are looking for safety.

drivers.name: Copper
drivers.note: “Dr. Copper”: rising copper = traders expect more growth.

drivers.name: Bitcoin
drivers.note: Trades all weekend and night: a read on risk appetite while Wall Street is shut.

drivers.name: S&P 500 vs 200-day
drivers.note: Below the 200-day = long-term downtrend: rallies have tended to get sold.

drivers.name: Stocks above 200-day
drivers.note: How many big US stocks are in their own uptrend.

drivers.name: VIX
drivers.note: Below 16 calm, above 25 nervous, above 30 fear.

drivers.name: VIX curve
drivers.note: Inverted (above 1): traders pay more for protection this month than for later months. Usually only in sell-offs.

drivers.name: Market mood
drivers.note: Neutral: the site's 0–100 fear/greed gauge from 10 readings. Extremes often mark turning points, so it sets the tone rather than the direction.

levels.name: SPY gamma flip
levels.note: Above it dealers calm moves down; below it they speed them up. Was 734 before the open.

levels.name: SPY call wall
levels.note: Biggest call position: often acts as a ceiling. Was 720 before the open.

levels.name: SPY call wall by today's volume
levels.note: Where today's new call trading is concentrated: shows the ceiling shifting during the session.

levels.name: SPY put wall by today's volume
levels.note: Where today's new put trading is concentrated: shows the floor shifting during the session.

levels.name: SPY put wall
levels.note: Biggest put position: often acts as a floor; a break can speed up selling.

scenarios.text: If SPY breaks below 700 (put wall), selling can speed up.
Above 715 (call wall) is where rallies often stall.
Yesterday's S&P 500 range was 6,970–7,165: a break of either end is the first real sign of direction.

tips: Size smaller than usual and use the “wrong if” level on every alert.
Avoid opening new trades just before the release time.
3 of the 6 Focus setups point the same way as the lean (3 long, 3 short).
Crypto: fear & greed 13 (Extreme Fear), Bitcoin −0.2% in 24h, funding 0.005%.
